title: MongoDB delivery and readback: clear, write, read back in one project
proves: a project declares one MongoDB client in the entry and uses it in three steps: clear the collection, write the orders, read them back
a normal run writes 12 documents and the readback returns 12 rows; a second run clears first and gives the same rows
the run checks values: an <assert> on every readback row (status set and amount range); a failed assert stops a normal run (negative run_assert_status_set_too_small)
Build reads the collection (seed.json, 12 documents) and proves the readback product against it; it isolates the write and skips the clear, so it does not prove that the load wrote the documents
the collection needs no schema: the test only fills it from db/seed.json before Build
the literal count on the readback works around #493 and is marked in the XML
this project needs the MongoDB service: it runs in the external-service test job

negatives.name: run_assert_status_set_too_small
negatives.expected: The collection holds a status that the load does not write
negatives.run_error: The collection holds a status that the load does not write
